newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies pare losses but end down.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies pare losses but end down.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures pared sharp early losses but remained pressured from negative fundamental and technical factors to close lower, traders said.
Hog futures closed 0.875 to 0.175 lower with April off most at 68.275 cents. Pork bellies finished 2.900 to 1.300 lower with May off 1.975 at 73.300 cents.

April hog futures fell to its lowest price level since October 25 before finding short covering support. Pressure stemmed from the weak tone to cash hogs and continued lighter than expected demand for pork products, traders said.
"They're (pork products) still suffering from poor demand," said Dan Vaught, livestock analyst for AG Edwards.
"You have all the ham buying done for Easter and with beef still looking like its dominating buying from the grocery stores, it just doesn't leave pork a whole lot of places to go," Vaught said.
Vaught also noted that exports of pork are seen running below year ago levels. Japanese demand for frozen pork will not increase until summer when the "gate" tariff is dropped, he added.
Hog futures were also technically weak, touching off sell stops under 68.700 cents in April and heading down to lowest levels in five months, traders said.
Latest CME lean hog index was off $0.05 to $66.91 per cwt.

R.J. O'Brien and Rand Financials notably sold April while Prudential Securities sold June on the break. ABN Chicago Corp bought April and locals bought June later to stem the setback. Rand later spread long April/short June, pit sources said.
In hog options, volatility was firm with put buying on the early break. Call buying developed later as the market looked for a bottom and futures recovered somewhat, pit sources said.

Pork belly futures remained under pressure from Tuesday's bearish CME weekly out-of-town storage report, but also pared losses late on some short covering that developed following two days of sharp declines. Sell stops added to the early setback before the short covering developed, traders said.

CME reported the net in-movement at approved warehouses last week at 2.486 million lbs, above the high end of early estimates of 1.0 to 2.0 million lbs. Certified deliverable stocks also continued to rise, they said.
Prudential, LFG, Rand, RBH and R.J. O'Brien sold before R.J. O'Brien and LFG turned buyers, pit sources said.
